finding: New `else if !canon.is_file()` (plus the empty-path filter at 1146/1103) makes `validate_for_install` REJECT states that previously validated green. Because `validate_for_install` is re-run on EVERY launch (runner.rs:1248 spawn_run, runner.rs:1552 resume_run), this is a behaviour regression for already-installed workflows, and it is silent for one class the diff never considers: a MOCKED step. runner.rs:758-768 short-circuits a step with `mock:` (or `force_mocks`) through `run_mock_step` BEFORE any dispatcher runs, so the prompt_file is never read. State that exposes it: a dev workflow (`is_dev=true`) with `- id: s, kind: llm, mock: {...}, prompt_file: "prompts/"` (a directory) or `prompt_file: ""`. Before: installed, launched, mock served, run SUCCEEDED. After: spawn_run returns 400 WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING / WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING and no run row is created at all. Same shape for a non-mocked broken step late in the DAG: previously the run started and earlier steps' outputs/artifacts were persisted before the step failed; now nothing runs and the failure surfaces as a launch-endpoint 400 instead of a failed run in history.

The docstring asserts INV-1 in BOTH directions — "a definition the validator reports green cannot fail here, and one it reports red cannot quietly succeed here". The second half is false. `load_raw_prompt` does no path-shape or confinement check whatsoever: `bundle_root.join(rel)` + `read_to_string`. `load_raw_prompt("s", bundle, &None, &Some("../../etc/passwd".into()))` returns Ok(<contents of /etc/passwd>) on any box where it is world-readable, while the validator reports WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE (validate.rs:1150-1157). Same for a bundle-internal symlink that resolves outside the root: validator → WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE (validate.rs:1168), runner → Ok. The invariant holds only because validate_for_install happens to be called first; nothing in dispatch enforces it. TEST-1's `files` array (dispatch.rs:1961-1967) contains None / "" / real.md / adir / nope.md — i.e. it excludes exactly the two cells that falsify the property, while its doc claims it walks "the whole authorable state space". Adding Some("../../etc/passwd") to that array turns TEST-1 red today.

The new directory branch reuses code WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING, and validate.rs:1181 asserts "Reuses the existing code, so the builder's author-facing copy needs no new entry." That is wrong: the copy for that code reads "This step points at a prompt file that isn't in the workflow — add the file, or type the prompt in directly." For `prompt_file: "prompts/adir"` the file-ish thing IS in the workflow and the remedy "add the file" is both false and unactionable — the author must instead point at a FILE inside that directory. This is precisely the false-author-facing-reason class (INV-6 / the builder's own DESIGN 2.5 rule) that the rest of this branch exists to eliminate, reintroduced by the reuse. Note the diff DID mint distinct copy for UNSAFE vs ESCAPE on exactly this reasoning (validationCopy.ts:106-114), so the precedent for a new entry is already in the file.

The new comment claims the padding rewrite is "RTL-correct", but the fix only converted the ADDON's own padding to logical (`ps`/`pe`). `InputGroup` itself (input-group.tsx:17, tokens `has-[>[data-align=inline-end]]:[&>input]:pr-1.5` and `has-[>[data-align=inline-start]]:[&>input]:pl-1.5`) still compensates the INPUT with PHYSICAL padding keyed off the LOGICAL `data-align` attribute. Before this change both halves were physical, so they were consistently wrong under RTL and cancelled out; now they disagree. State that exposes it: load the gallery with `?dir=rtl` (GALLERY_DIRS supports it, `_gallery.ts:53`) and render a combobox — the addon moves to the visual left (order-last + logical padding) while the input's extra 6px of padding stays on the visual right, i.e. on the side with no addon. The change makes the RTL rendering worse, not better, and the new spec cannot see it because it only loads `/gallery.html` with no `dir` param (input-group-overflow.spec.ts:95).

The new spec settles the gallery with a fixed `page.waitForTimeout(1500)` after `domcontentloaded` (also at :146). `canon.is_file()` conflates 'not a regular file' with 'stat failed': `Path::is_file` swallows every io::Error and returns false. REJECTED: DESIGN §3's descoped items being silently folded in. The addon base keeps `py-1.5` (the 36px-in-32px VERTICAL containment §3 defers), `block-start`/`block-end` keep `px-2.5`, and the pre-existing arbitrary `[&>kbd]:rounded-[calc(var(--radius)-5px)]` is untouched. REJECTED as a finding against this change: `workflow::models::tests::job_kind_parses_round_trips_and_is_orthogonal` also fails on the audited tree (`unknown variant 'subagent', expected one of 'workflow','sandbox_exec','sub_agent'`). models.rs is not in parent2.diff and the failure is unrelated to the prompt rule — a pre-existing baseline failure, not caused by this branch. Recorded so it is not conflated with the humanisation-guard regression, which IS caused by it.

stat-before-open FIFO guard is TOCTOU-bypassable, and the comment at :1296-1301 asserts it is not. `std::fs::metadata(&canon)` (:1302) and `open_no_follow(&canon)` (:1312) are two INDEPENDENT path resolutions with no shared fd. For run_from_workspace / validate_from_workspace the bundle_root IS the sandbox's RW bind mount (workflow_mcp/tools.rs:571 sets extracted_path = resolve_conversation_workspace_dir() = workflow_workspace_root()/<conv_id> = code_sandbox workspace_root/<conv_id>, RW-bind-mounted at /home/sandboxuser per code_sandbox/tools/files.rs:33). Concrete input: model writes workflow.yaml with `prompt_file: p.md` plus a regular p.md, then runs in the sandbox `while :; do rm -f p.md; mkfifo p.md; rm -f p.md; cp orig p.md; done` while repeatedly calling the workflow MCP validate/run verb. On the interleaving where metadata() sees the regular file and open() sees the FIFO, open(2) O_RDONLY on a FIFO with no writer BLOCKS FOREVER (O_NOFOLLOW does not affect FIFOs). Each win parks one thread permanently. Fix: open with O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW first, then fstat(2) the fd and reject non-regular, then clear O_NONBLOCK — i.e. make the guard operate on the fd, not on a re-resolved path.

O_NOFOLLOW guards only the FINAL path component, so the confinement check is still TOCTOU-defeatable via an INTERMEDIATE directory swap — contradicting the doc at :1174-1178 which claims the window is closed. After canonicalize() (:1287) and the starts_with confinement test (:1293), both metadata() (:1302) and open_no_follow() (:1312) re-walk the whole path from `/`, following symlinks on every component except the last. Concrete state: bundle_root is the sandbox-writable conversation workspace (see the previous finding); model creates `prompts/passwd` (regular, so canonicalize+starts_with pass) and `prompt_file: prompts/passwd`; a racing sandbox process does `mv prompts prompts.bak; ln -s /etc prompts` between the canonicalize and the open. The server (running OUTSIDE the sandbox, as the server uid, on the HOST filesystem view) then opens /etc/passwd: O_NOFOLLOW is satisfied because the final component `passwd` is a real file. Contents land in the LLM prompt, the step prompt log (dispatch.rs:196 log_io::write_text_log) and any validator finding. Fix: openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS) against a dirfd of the canonical root, or a per-component O_NOFOLLOW dirfd walk.

read_prompt_file is synchronous, blocking file I/O and is now reached from `validate_for_install` on plain tokio WORKER threads with no spawn_blocking. dispatch.rs:137 correctly wraps its call, but every validator caller does not: workflow_mcp/tools.rs:539 (`async fn load_and_validate_workspace`), workflow/runner.rs:1248 (`spawn_run`), workflow/runner.rs:1552 (`resume_run`), workflow/handlers/dev.rs:564, hub/handlers.rs:2187 — all async fns calling it directly. Before this change check_prompt_files only did canonicalize(); it now does metadata + open + read of up to 1 MiB per prompt_file. Combined with the FIFO race above, a handful of wins park the runtime's worker threads permanently and the whole server stops scheduling. Even benignly, a slow/NFS-backed bundle now stalls a worker for the duration of the read.

The non-unix branch of open_no_follow is NOT equivalent: `std::fs::File::open` follows symlinks and NTFS reparse points, so on Windows even the FINAL-component swap (the one case the unix branch does close) escapes confinement, and read_prompt_file's doc at :1257-1282 makes an unqualified confinement claim. The `#[cfg(not(unix))]` fallback is silent — no runtime warning, no compensating check (e.g. FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT / re-verifying the opened handle's final path via GetFinalPathNameByHandleW). The repo ships and supports Windows (CLAUDE.md, wsl2 sandbox backend), so this is a live platform, not a theoretical one.

MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES bounds ONE file, but the loop that consumes it is unbounded, so the doc's claim (:1163-1169) that the cap prevents 'unbounded work' on every launch does not hold in aggregate. check_prompt_files iterates every step (:1401) and validate_collecting (:582-586) runs check_steps_shape and check_prompt_files unconditionally — the >50-step cap at :656 only PUSHES a finding, it never short-circuits. Concrete input: a workflow.yaml with 100k steps each carrying `prompt_file: big.md` (a 1 MiB file) makes one validate call perform 100 GB of blocking reads plus 100k × 1 MiB of transient allocation, on a tokio worker (see the concurrency finding). Author-controlled, and reachable from the MCP workspace verbs with no install required.

`rel.contains('\\')` is a NEW rejection with no migration path, and it silently breaks existing data on Windows. Previously check_prompt_files rejected only `..` and a leading `/`; a Windows-authored bundle with `prompt_file: "prompts\\task.md"` validated AND ran correctly on Windows (PathBuf::join honours backslash there). It now hard-fails WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE at install, at spawn_run (runner.rs:1248) AND at resume_run (runner.rs:1552) — an already-installed, previously-working workflow becomes unlaunchable, and a suspended run becomes unresumable. The rationale comment (:1239-1242) argues for cross-platform determinism but does not acknowledge that it retroactively invalidates installed bundles.

Four new failure classes now block resume_run of an IN-FLIGHT run, which previously only required the prompt file to exist. resume_run re-runs validate_for_install, which now goes through read_prompt_file, so a durably-suspended run (e.g. parked on an elicit gate) refuses to resume if its prompt file has since become zero-byte (PromptFileError::Empty, validate.rs:1325), >1 MiB (TooLarge, :1309), non-UTF-8 (:1323), or a non-regular file (:1304). For run_from_workspace runs the bundle root is the model-writable sandbox workspace, so the model's own later `>` truncation of its prompt file kills the resume of its own suspended run. A zero-byte prompt file previously produced a (degenerate but successful) run; this is a behaviour change on existing data with no compatibility shim.

The spawn_blocking await is outside the module's own stated cancellation contract, and dropping its JoinHandle does not abort the blocking task. dispatch.rs:4-8 states every dispatcher 'wraps the blocking await in tokio::select! { _, cancel }'; resolve_prompt is awaited bare at dispatch.rs:186 (LlmDispatcher), :397 (LlmMapDispatcher) and agent_dispatch.rs:1101 — none under a cancel select. So (a) a run cancelled while the prompt file is being read cannot interrupt it, and (b) when the future IS dropped (client disconnect / run cancel / RUN_WALL_CLOCK timeout at runner.rs:1128), tokio does not cancel a spawn_blocking task: a read hung on the FIFO race above leaks a blocking-pool thread for the process lifetime, invisibly, with no run left to report it.

PromptFileError::code() (:1196) and ::layer() (:1207) are `pub` with ZERO callers anywhere in the tree (verified by grep across src-app/**/*.rs — the only hits are the prose at :1337/:1341). prompt_file_finding (:1345) deliberately re-writes the same variant→code/layer mapping as literals. That is two independent copies of one rule with nothing asserting they agree — exactly the 'two places decide separately' shape this whole change exists to eliminate, reintroduced inside the change itself. Also CODING_GUIDELINES §15 (pub fn with no consumer; the `pub` also suppresses the dead_code lint that would otherwise flag it). If the textual drift guard truly needs literals, code()/layer() should be deleted or a unit test should pin `prompt_file_finding(&e,..).code == e.code()` for every variant.

The submodule fix was applied to only one of the two visual workflows. visual-snapshots.yml:42 is a bare `actions/checkout@v4` (no `submodules: recursive`) followed by `npm ci`, while root package.json declares workspaces ['src-app/ui','src-app/desktop/ui','sdk/packages/*']. By the diff's own reasoning (visual-tests.yml:37-43) sdk/ therefore checks out empty, the sdk/packages/* workspace links cannot resolve, and `npm ci` fails before anything runs. This is the Layer B (pixel-baseline) job — i.e. the workflow a maintainer must use to bless baselines for the very kit regression this change is about is structurally unable to run.

`rel.contains("..")` is a SUBSTRING test, not a component test, so it rejects legitimate bundle-relative paths whose filenames merely contain two dots: `prompts/v1..2/task.md`, `task..md`, `spec..draft.md`. Because read_prompt_file is now also on the RUN path, such a workflow is not just un-installable but reports a SECURITY finding (WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE, whose UI copy at validationCopy.ts:105 says 'written as a location elsewhere on the machine') for a file that is plainly inside the bundle — an unactionable false accusation. A Component::ParentDir scan (as workflow/workspace.rs:73-83 already does for `dir`) would be both correct and consistent with the sibling confinement helper in this same crate.

`bundle_root.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| bundle_root.to_path_buf())` silently swallows the error (CODING_GUIDELINES §6) and then compares a fully-canonical `canon` against a possibly non-canonical `root_canon` at :1293. The two operands are no longer in the same normalisation space, so `starts_with` answers a different question than the one intended. It happens to fail SAFE today (a relative or unresolvable root yields a false Escape, not a false pass) only because :1287 would already have returned for the same reason — i.e. the fallback is load-bearing-looking dead code whose safety is incidental, not established. Either propagate the error or assert the invariant.

The two TooLarge sites report incomparable numbers. :1310 reports the file's real size; :1321 reports `buf.len()`, which the take(MAX+1) at :1316 has clamped to exactly 1048577. So the growth path always tells the author 'prompt_file X is 1048577 bytes, over the 1048576-byte limit' regardless of whether the file is 1 MiB + 1 byte or 5 GiB — the message reads like a trivial 1-byte overage and misdirects the remedy. Report the stat size, or say 'over the limit' without a fabricated count.

The rewritten WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING copy enumerates four causes ('missing, be a folder rather than a file, be empty, or not be text') but the code now also covers a FIFTH: PromptFileError::TooLarge (validate.rs:1201 maps TooLarge to this same code). An author whose prompt file exceeds 1 MiB is told to check whether it is a folder or empty — neither is true, and the actual remedy (shrink the file) is not offered. The humanised copy replaces the backend `message()`, so the byte-count detail from validate.rs:1225 never reaches them.

read_prompt_file and check_prompt_file_shape are both `pub` and neither rejects an EMPTY `rel`, even though 'empty means absent' is the central rule this change introduces. `read_prompt_file(root, "")` reaches `bundle_root.join("")` == bundle_root, canonicalizes and confinement-passes, and is only stopped by the incidental `is_file()` at :1304 (yielding a misleading 'cannot be read from the bundle: not a regular file'). The emptiness rule lives solely in the two callers (prompt_file_ref at :1137 and prompt_source at :1114), so a third caller of this pub API silently reintroduces the exact bug the change fixed. Reject `rel.is_empty()` inside check_prompt_file_shape.

The controlClearanceDelta assertion (`misplaced = groups.filter(g => delta !== null && delta >= 0)` must be empty) is coupled to an element-TYPE selector it does not control, so it will false-fail the moment a legitimate consumer appears. The tightening rule on the InputGroup root is `has-[>[data-align=inline-end]]:[&>input]:pe-1.5` (sdk/packages/kit/src/shadcn/input-group.tsx:17) — an `input` type selector — while the probe selects `[data-slot="input-group-control"]`, which InputGroupTextarea (input-group.tsx:167) also carries on a `<textarea>`. Any InputGroup pairing an inline addon with a textarea control gets delta == 0, trips `>= 0`, and reports 'physical padding keyed off a logical attribute' — a diagnosis that is simply false for that cell. It passes today only because InputGroupTextarea has zero consumers in the tree.

REJECTED: 'the size check can be defeated by growth between stat and read'. It cannot. meta.len() is checked against MAX at :1309 BEFORE Vec::with_capacity(meta.len()) at :1314, so the pre-allocation is bounded at 1 MiB; the read itself is bounded independently by Read::take(MAX+1) at :1316; and the post-read re-check at :1320 converts any growth into TooLarge. A file that grows from 100 bytes to 10 GiB between the stat and the read yields TooLarge, not an OOM. The only defect here is the misleading byte count in the message (logged separately).

REJECTED: 'the author-facing error text leaks a host path'. PromptFileError::message() interpolates only `rel` (the author's own bundle-relative string) and never `canon`, `resolved` or `bundle_root`. The `Unreadable(why)` payloads come from std::fs io::Error Display, which for canonicalize/metadata/open/read carries the errno text only ('No such file or directory (os error 2)') — std::fs deliberately does not attach the path (unlike fs_err/anyhow). String::from_utf8's error carries a byte offset. Verified across all five construction sites (:1288, :1303, :1305, :1312, :1319, :1324).

REJECTED: 'the shape check can be bypassed with unicode / normalisation / empty-segment / dot-segment / Windows-absolute tricks'. Probed: U+2024 and other dot homoglyphs are not `..` to any kernel; overlong UTF-8 is unrepresentable in a Rust &str so `rel` is always well-formed; `.`/empty segments (`a/./b`, `a//b`) are inert; the drive-letter test at :1243-1246 is byte-indexed and correct (`C:` at index 0-1, alphabetic first byte); UNC and `\\?\` forms are caught by the backslash reject. On Linux only `/` and NUL are structurally special, and NUL yields an InvalidInput io::Error at the syscall boundary. Crucially, the shape check is not the confinement boundary anyway — canonicalize + component-wise starts_with at :1287-1295 is, and Path::starts_with is component-based, so the classic `/root/bundle-evil` string-prefix bypass does not apply.

REJECTED: 'a symlinked bundle root, or a relative path that canonicalizes back inside via a symlink, defeats confinement'. Both operands of the starts_with test are produced by canonicalize (:1287, :1290), so a symlinked bundle root resolves identically on both sides and compares correctly; a bundle-internal symlink that resolves back inside the root is intentionally allowed and is genuinely inside. Separately, a symlink or FIFO cannot arrive in an INSTALLED bundle at all: hub/bundle.rs:567-575 rejects every tar entry that is not Regular or Dir ('symlinks / devices / FIFOs / hardlinks rejected'). The live risk is only the sandbox-writable workspace root, covered by the two TOCTOU findings above.

REJECTED: 'a caller of the changed signatures was missed'. load_raw_prompt's signature change (StepDef+RunContext -> &str+&Path) has exactly two call sites, both updated: dispatch.rs:92 (resolve_prompt) and dispatch.rs:397 (LlmMapDispatcher). resolve_prompt itself keeps its signature and its third consumer, agent_dispatch.rs:1101, is therefore correct unchanged. All three prompt-bearing kinds (Llm, LlmMap, Agent) route through it; StepConfig::prompt_fields (validate.rs:285) is exhaustive over StepConfig with no `_` arm, so a new prompt-bearing kind is a compile error. check_prompt_files' old inline match was the only other reader of the pair and it was migrated (:1404).

`StepConfig::prompt_source(&self)` has ZERO callers — production or test — anywhere in server/, desktop/ or tests/. rustc confirms it: `cargo test --lib -p ziee --no-run` now emits `warning: method `prompt_source` is never used --> server/src/modules/workflow/validate.rs:281:12`, a NEW warning this diff introduces (the other 5 dead-code warnings are in chat/control_mcp/scheduler and pre-date it). Violates CODING_GUIDELINES §15 ('every new public fn with a side effect has a production caller'). Worse, its own doc-comment sells it as the safe wrapper — 'Preferred over calling `prompt_source(a, b)` directly: the two arguments there are adjacent, same-typed and opposite in meaning, so swapping them compiles and turns the prompt text into a file path' — yet BOTH real call sites (dispatch.rs:130 `match prompt_source(prompt, prompt_file)` and validate.rs:714 `match prompt_source(prompt, prompt_file)`) call the free function with exactly that hazardous shape. The mitigation was written and then not adopted.

`PromptFileError::code()` and `PromptFileError::layer()` (validate.rs ~1196 and ~1207) have zero callers. `prompt_file_finding` deliberately re-writes the SAME variant→code and variant→layer mapping with string literals, and its doc explains why (the humanisation_contract scanner only reads literal constructor args). So the diff ships two independent encodings of one mapping, with nothing pinning them to each other and no test on either — precisely the 'two places decide separately' shape the whole change exists to eliminate. Either delete both methods or make `prompt_file_finding` the only mapping and teach the scanner about it.

`check_prompt_file_shape` grew two NEW rejection clauses — the Windows drive-letter test (`rel.as_bytes().get(1) == b':' && [0].is_ascii_alphabetic()`, line 1309) and `rel.contains('\\')` (line 1315) — and NEITHER has a single test. Grepped server/src and server/tests: no test string contains a backslash path or a `C:` path. Deleting either clause turns nothing red. The diff's own justification for them is cross-platform correctness ('a bundle authored on one OS is validated and run on another'), i.e. exactly the case no test on this platform will otherwise reach.

The new DoS ceiling is entirely untested. `MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES` (1170), the `meta.len() > MAX` stat guard, the `Read::take(MAX+1)` bound, the post-read `buf.len() > MAX` re-check, and `PromptFileError::TooLarge` have no test anywhere (`grep -rn 'TooLarge|MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES' tests/ src/modules/workflow | grep -i test` → nothing). `PromptFileError::TooLarge` is therefore a variant that is constructible but never observed, and every one of those four lines could be deleted with the suite still green. Same for `open_no_follow`/`O_NOFOLLOW`, whose whole stated purpose is a TOCTOU window no test opens. These are the security-shaped additions in the diff and they are the least covered.

`validate_def_prompt_source_verdicts` — the FIRST assertion (`prompt: ""` beside `prompt_file: "prompts/task.md"` ⇒ neither WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH nor WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING) has NO production revert that turns it red. It was already green on the pre-fix code: the old rule was `has_prompt = prompt.as_ref().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).is_some()` (false for `""`) and `has_file = prompt_file.is_some()` (true), so neither code fired — that GREEN verdict beside a failing run is literally the bug being fixed. Reverting `prompt_source`, `prompt_file_ref`, `check_prompt_files` or `load_raw_prompt` all leave it passing. It documents intent; it guards nothing.

Same test asserts a claim strictly wider than what it exercises. Its doc-comment says 'INV-1: a def this endpoint reports clean must run, and one it rejects must not quietly run' and headlines 'the two prompt states that used to validate GREEN and then fail the RUN' — but the test only POSTs to /workflows/validate-def and reads `errors[].code`. It never dispatches, never calls `load_raw_prompt`, and /validate-def has no materialized bundle, so it is structurally incapable of observing either half of a validate↔run disagreement. Only the SECOND assertion (`prompt_file: ""` ⇒ WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING) is falsifiable here, and it is falsifiable against the validator alone.

The block labelled 'Control:' does NOT inject the defect that was fixed. It posts `prompt: "inline"` + `prompt_file: "prompts/task.md"` and asserts WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH — a verdict that is byte-identical before and after the change (old rule: has_prompt=true, has_file=true ⇒ BOTH). Its stated job is 'so the first assertion above is not passing because the check stopped firing', but the first assertion is itself unfalsifiable (see the prior finding), so the control guards a non-guard. A control that injected the actual defect would be a def with `prompt: ""` + `prompt_file:` asserted to RUN, which this endpoint cannot express.

No integration or E2E test ever executes a workflow RUN with a `prompt_file:` step. `grep -rln prompt_file src-app/server/tests/` returns exactly ONE file (builder_validate_def_test.rs), which never runs a workflow. The whole runner half of INV-1 is unit-only: TEST-1/TEST-6 call `load_raw_prompt` directly against a tempdir, never through `resolve_prompt` (dispatch.rs:92), `LlmDispatcher::dispatch`, `LlmMapDispatcher` (dispatch.rs:397) or `agent_dispatch.rs:1101` — all three of which this diff re-pointed at the new loader. A regression in the re-plumbing (wrong bundle root passed, `spawn_blocking` result mis-mapped, agent path missed) would be invisible.

`client_prompt_file_predicate_mirrors_prompt_source` is one-directional but documented as bidirectional. It text-scans `promptSuppliedByFile`'s TS body for `length > 0` / `!== ''` / `length !== 0` and for the absence of `.trim()` — i.e. it pins the TS side to hard-coded literals. It never reads `prompt_source` or `prompt_file_ref`. Its doc claims it will 'fail the BACKEND suite on drift' between the two implementations, but adding `.trim()` to `prompt_source` (the Rust side) leaves it green. (TEST-2 does catch that specific change, so the CLASS is covered — the guard's own claim is what is false, and a reader relying on it will not add the Rust-side pin.) Secondary brittleness: the assertion is substring-based, so `pf.length>0` (no spaces, e.g. after a formatter change) fails it spuriously, and `pf.trimEnd()` passes the no-trim check.

`prompt_codes_list_covers_every_prompt_verdict_the_validator_emits` enforces only half of what its own doc demands. It asserts `VALIDATION_CODES ∩ prefix('WORKFLOW_PROMPT') == PROMPT_CODES`; the doc says 'add the new code to PROMPT_CODES *and* give the matrix an input that produces it', but nothing checks the second clause. Adding a code to both lists satisfies the guard while TEST-1's matrix never produces it, which is the exact silent-shrink the guard was written to prevent. A cheap fix: have TEST-1 collect the union of codes it observed and assert it equals PROMPT_CODES. Secondary: the filter is the literal prefix `WORKFLOW_PROMPT`, so a future prompt verdict named e.g. `WORKFLOW_STEP_PROMPT_*` escapes the guard entirely. Also note WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE is produced by the matrix only on unix (the `prompts/escape.md` symlink is `#[cfg(unix)]`); on Windows that row degrades to FILE_MISSING and the code is never exercised.

The spec's coverage note overstates the population it actually measures, and its two anti-vacuity guards do not catch the shortfall. Measured live against the running gallery (:5397, 390px and 1280px, ltr and rtl): the page contains exactly TWO `[data-slot="input-group"]` elements, BOTH carry only an `inline-end` addon, and BOTH have a `> button` child. So there are ZERO `inline-start` rows and ZERO bare (no-button/no-kbd) rows. The doc claims measurement 'for BOTH `inline-start` and `inline-end` addons ... measured in the WRITING direction — the two variants are written as a symmetric pair, so a guard on one of them lets the other rot' and that the spec 'exercises the `has-[>button]` branch and the bare branch'. Neither is true today. `expect(groups.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` and `expect(groups.filter(hasButtonChild).length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` are both satisfied by that same 2-row population, so the `ps-2` bare branch and the entire `inline-start` variant (including its `[&>input]:ps-1.5` clearance rule) could be reverted to a negative physical margin with this spec still green.

The falsifiability control covers the overflow + containment probes only; the `controlClearanceDelta` probe — the one the spec says 'is the part an RTL render is uniquely able to observe' and 'without this the RTL rows would merely re-assert the LTR overflow property' — has no injected control. Re-injecting REVERTED_RULE (a negative addon margin) does not move `controlClearanceDelta` at all, so the assertion that carries the RTL rows' entire independent value is never demonstrated to be able to fail. I verified by hand that it IS falsifiable: injecting the physical equivalent of the reverted `[&>input]:pr-1.5` (`[data-slot=input-group-control]{padding-left:10px;padding-right:6px}`) leaves LTR at delta −4/−4 (0 misplaced) and flips RTL to +4/+4 (2 misplaced ⇒ red). So the probe works; the spec just does not prove it.

`REVERTED_RULE` is documented as 'The exact rule that was removed' and the control's comment says 'exactly as the kit had it', but it injects `margin-inline-end:-0.3rem` (LOGICAL) whereas the removed kit rule was `has-[>kbd]/has-[>button]:mr-[-0.3rem]` (PHYSICAL `margin-right`). They coincide in LTR, which is the only direction the control runs, so the control is sound today — but the physical/logical distinction is the diff's headline rationale, and the constant asserts a byte-equality that does not hold. A physical `margin-right` revert is in fact NOT caught by the containment probe in RTL (the margin lands on the addon's inner side), only by the clearance probe.

`openWithAddons` deliberately replaces a wall-clock settle with two positive DOM signals, but drops the one the shared helper `openGallery` (tests/e2e/visual/_gallery.ts:64) waits on: `root.dir === dir`. It waits only for `gallery-root` visible plus 'some addon with a > button child exists'. Since `probeGroups` derives `rtl` from `getComputedStyle(el).direction`, a run that measured before ThemeProvider applied `dir` would silently produce LTR measurements under an RTL test name and still pass every assertion — the RTL rows would degrade to duplicate LTR rows with nothing to report it. Latent, not live: I confirmed `documentElement.dir === 'rtl'` and computed direction rtl at probe time today. Add `root.dir === dir` to the waitForFunction (or assert `groups.every(g => g.rtl)` in the RTL rows).

TEST-6 asserts `err.contains("without '..'")` for BOTH `prompts/../prompts/real.md` and `/etc/passwd`, pinning an author-facing message ('prompt_file '<rel>' must be a bundle-relative path without ..') that names the wrong defect for an absolute path — and, after this diff, for a backslash path and a `C:`-drive path too, since all four collapse into `PromptFileError::Unsafe` with one message. The test now makes that mis-description load-bearing: splitting the message per cause would fail it. The paired UI copy (`WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE`, validationCopy.ts) is generic enough to cover it, so this is a message-precision issue the test freezes rather than a user-visible break.

`assert_eq!(ran_ok, 18, "the matrix must contain rows that legitimately RUN, or the implication holds vacuously")` is an exact-equality tripwire doing double duty as an anti-vacuity guard AND an undeclared behavioural assertion. The doc's justification ("acceptable because the untrusted writer runs on a Linux kernel on ALL THREE host platforms") is a non-sequitur: confinement is performed by the SERVER's kernel, not the sandbox guest's, and on macOS the workspace dir the guest can write to is a macOS host directory resolved by macOS. That is the exact behaviour the comment three lines below claims the code avoids ("a symlink that stays inside the bundle still resolves, exactly as the non-Linux fallback allows... RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS is deliberately NOT set... so Linux and non-Linux would disagree about whether a bundle is valid"). A model-authored workflow.yaml in its own sandbox workspace can therefore declare N steps (N bounded only by the size of the workflow.yaml the model writes, which is read with an uncapped tokio::fs::read_to_string) all pointing at ONE 1 MiB prompt file, and each validate_from_workspace / run_from_workspace call re-reads it N times - ~25 GB of reads for ~1 MB of YAML, executed synchronously on a tokio worker (see the unconverted-caller finding). openat2's EAGAIN is not handled. openat2(2) documents EAGAIN specifically for RESOLVE_BENEATH/RESOLVE_IN_ROOT when the kernel could not prove a '..' or symlink did not escape the root because of a racing rename, and states "the caller may wish to retry the operation". That is precisely the scenario this function was written for (a sandbox renaming directories under the bundle root while the resolution runs). It falls into the `_ =>` arm and becomes PromptFileError::Unreadable("Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)") -> WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING, whose author-facing copy says the file "may be missing, be a folder rather than a file, be empty, be too large, or not be text" - none of which is true. A benign concurrent rename in the workspace thus fails a run with a misleading, unactionable verdict instead of retrying.

Only ENOSYS triggers open_confined_fallback, but a missing openat2 does not always surface as ENOSYS. A seccomp filter that does not list openat2 returns EPERM under Docker's default profile (openat2 was only added to moby's default seccomp profile in 20.10.10), and some sandboxed runtimes (gVisor/runsc, older qemu-user, restrictive systemd SystemCallFilter=) return EPERM or EINVAL. Any of those lands in the `_ =>` arm as PromptFileError::Unreadable, so EVERY prompt_file: in the deployment - installed bundles included - starts failing validate_for_install with WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING and workflows that ran yesterday stop launching, with copy that blames the author's file. The fallback exists precisely to make "the kernel/runtime cannot do openat2" a deployment fact rather than an author error; the errno set it keys on is too narrow to deliver that.

read_prompt_file_refuses_a_bundle_root_that_became_a_symlink is gated #[cfg(unix)] although the behaviour it asserts exists only in the #[cfg(target_os = "linux")] openat2 branch. On macOS (a supported build/test host for this repo) open_confined is open_confined_fallback, which resolves the swapped root and returns Ok("HOST SECRET"), so the test's expect_err panics: the suite goes red on macOS rather than guarding anything. The same applies on any Linux kernel <5.6 via the ENOSYS path. Either gate it target_os="linux", or give the fallback the anchor guard it is asserting.

Silent behaviour change for already-installed data. spawn_run/resume_run re-validate against the real bundle, and read_prompt_file now hard-rejects four file states the previous existence-only check accepted: >1 MiB (TooLarge), non-UTF-8, zero-byte (Empty), and - via the widened check_prompt_file_shape - any path containing a backslash (a legal filename character on Linux, previously accepted and readable). A workflow installed before this change with any of those launches with WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING and, on the resume_run path, an in-flight durable run becomes permanently unresumable. The intent is documented in the new code, but nothing in the diff migrates or even surveys existing rows, and the author-facing copy does not distinguish "your file is 1.2 MiB" from "your file is missing" beyond the free-form message.

ELOOP is folded into PromptFileError::Escape together with EXDEV, so three distinct causes - a RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS rejection, an ordinary symlink loop / >40-link chain, and (per the O_NOFOLLOW finding) an ordinary in-bundle symlink - all report the security finding WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE, whose copy states the file "ends up outside the workflow once the location is followed". Only EXDEV actually means that. The comment acknowledges the conflation but the author-facing consequence (a false security verdict on a file that is inside the bundle) is not sound.

open_confined passes O_NOFOLLOW inside how.flags, so on Linux ANY final-component symlink fails with ELOOP and is mapped to PromptFileError::Escape -> WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE — including a symlink that stays INSIDE the bundle. Verified empirically with a direct openat2 probe (in-bundle 'link.md' -> 'real.md' returns ELOOP; 'sub/up.md' -> '../real.md' returns ELOOP; the real file returns OK). Three consequences: (1) a bundle whose prompt_file: is an in-bundle symlink used to validate GREEN and run (old code canonicalized, then read_to_string) and is now REFUSED — a THIRD re-verdict of a definition that used to install, where DESIGN §1 enumerates exactly two ('a size cap' and 'a platform-independent shape check') and says they are listed 'so they are part of the design rather than a side effect'; (2) the author is told the file 'ends up outside the workflow', which is false; (3) the non-Linux/pre-5.6 fallback canonicalizes BEFORE opening, so it resolves the symlink and ACCEPTS the same bundle — Linux and non-Linux disagree about whether a bundle is valid.

The comment on how.resolve states: 'RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS is deliberately NOT set: it would additionally refuse in-bundle symlinks, which are legitimate and which the fallback accepts, so Linux and non-Linux would disagree about whether a bundle is valid.' The O_NOFOLLOW set two lines above in how.flags produces exactly that refusal (measured: ELOOP on an in-bundle symlink) and exactly that disagreement, so the comment describes a property the code does not have. It is also contradicted inside this same diff by dispatch.rs's prompt_bundle() fixture comment, which says escape.md is 'a FINAL-component symlink (caught by O_NOFOLLOW alone)' — i.e. the author knows O_NOFOLLOW refuses final-component symlinks unconditionally.

check_prompt_files calls read_prompt_file once PER STEP with no memoization, and read_prompt_file is a bounded-but-real 1 MiB read. The step cap is 50 (validate.rs:683), so a ~1 KB workflow.yaml pointing 50 steps at one 1 MiB prompt file buys 50 MiB of blocking disk reads — on every install AND, via spawn_run/resume_run, on every launch. ITEM-16 introduced MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES precisely because 'the validator runs on every launch, so an uncapped read is author-controlled work and memory'; the per-step amplification reinstates a 50x multiple of that same work. (Concurrent edit in this worktree is adding a per-validation memo cache for exactly this.)
